messages.content: What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?

function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_genotype_frequency
function.description: Calculate the frequency of homozygous dominant genotype based on the allele frequency using Hardy Weinberg Principle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

allele_frequency.description: The frequency of the dominant allele in the population. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** such as β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels**: voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav), ligand‑gated NMDA receptor
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases**: EGFR, HER2
• **Integrins** (αβ heterodimers, e.g., α5β1)
• **Cadherins** (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels, e.g., Cx43)
• **Tetraspanins** (CD9, CD63) | | **Peripheral (non‑integral) proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via lipid anchors or interactions with integral proteins. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane stability)
• **Band‑3 protein** (anion exchanger, peripheral in red cells)
• **Glycophorin A** (glycoprotein, peripheral in erythrocytes)
• **MHC class I & II molecules** (present antigens; anchored by a short transmembrane segment but largely peripheral in function)
• **Signal transduction proteins**: Src family kinases, phospholipase C, etc. | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **GPI‑anchored CD59** (protects cells from complement)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **CD55 (decay‑accelerating factor)** | | **Extracellular matrix‑binding proteins** | Interact with the extracellular matrix and help mediate adhesion. | • **Fibronectin** (binds integrins)
• **Collagen‑binding integrins** (α2β1) | ### How to use this list - **Research**: If you’re studying a particular cell type, look up which of these proteins are expressed in that tissue (e.g., neurons have many ion channels and neurotransmitter receptors). - **Drug targeting**: Many drugs target GPCRs, ion channels, or receptor tyrosine kinases because they are accessible on the cell surface. - **Diagnostics**: Surface markers (e.g., CD antigens) are used in flow cytometry to identify cell populations. Feel free to ask for more details on any specific protein family or for a deeper dive into their structure and function!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like actin-binding proteins, ankyrin, spectrin. Provide a concise but informative answer. No function calls needed.
